title: The application segment Bypass setting and how it ranks

prose.text: The Bypass setting lets users reach an application without Private Access, and ranks against client forwarding policy and against other segments.

prose.label: Options.
prose.text: {{bypass-options}} {{cfp-implicit-forward}} Which console option each API value stands for is open {{gap:label-to-api-mapping}}. {{bypass-api-values}}

prose.text: {{bypass-beats-cfp}} {{bypass-domain-level}} {{same-fqdn-always}} Whether Always also outranks a more granular segment with a different FQDN is open {{gap:always-across-different-fqdns}}. How granularity is decided otherwise: [[zpa.app-segments.matching]].

checks.do: Whether any segment covering the same FQDN has Bypass set to Always, since that segment takes precedence over the others.

Whether the forwarding profile sends the user to Private Access at all, since Private Access evaluates the forwarding profile first and checks the application's Bypass setting when the profile specifies that the user must use Private Access.
Which of the API values ALWAYS, NEVER and ON_NET the tenant holds, read from the segment's bypassType.

bypass-options.statement: The Bypass setting offers Use Client Forwarding Policy (the default), Always, and On Corporate Network, which lets users bypass Private Access from a trusted network defined in the Zscaler Client Connector forwarding profile.

quotes: Use Client Forwarding Policy: This option is selected by default.
Always: If selected, users can always bypass Private Access when accessing an application.

On Corporate Network: If selected, users can bypass Private Access when accessing an application from a trusted network. Private Access checks if the user is on a trusted network defined in the Zscaler Client Connector forwarding profile.

cfp-implicit-forward.statement: With Use Client Forwarding Policy, if none of the client forwarding policy rules apply, or none are defined, access to the application is implicitly Forward to ZPA.

quotes: If none of the policy rules apply, then access to the application is implicitly set to Forward to ZPA.
This is also the case if you do not define any client forwarding policy rules at all within the Zscaler Admin Console.

bypass-beats-cfp.statement: The Bypass setting within an application segment always takes precedence over any newly added client forwarding policy rule.

quotes: The Bypass setting within an application segment always takes precedence over any newly added client forwarding policy rule.

same-fqdn-always.statement: If the same FQDN is defined in multiple application segments and one of them has Bypass set to Always, that application segment takes precedence.

quotes: if the same FQDN is defined in multiple application segments, and one of them has the Bypass setting set to Always, then that application segment takes precedence.

bypass-domain-level.statement: The Bypass setting is applied at the domain level; Private Access first evaluates the forwarding profile, and when the profile specifies that the user must use Private Access, it checks the application's Bypass setting.

quotes: The Bypass setting is applied at the domain level.
If the forwarding profile specifies that the user must use Private Access, then Private Access checks the application's Bypass setting
When a user requests access to an application, Private Access evaluates the forwarding profile.

bypass-api-values.statement: The API and the Terraform schema accept three `bypassType` values: `ALWAYS`, `NEVER` and `ON_NET`.

quotes: Description: "Indicates whether users can bypass ZPA to access applications.",

always-disables-reauth-bypass.statement: The AI-Powered Recommendations page's segment form says that if you select Always for the Bypass option, then Bypass during Reauthentication is automatically disabled and cannot be enabled.

quotes: If you select Always for the Bypass option, then Bypass during Reauthentication is automatically disabled and cannot be enabled.

reauth-bypass.statement: Bypass during Reauthentication, when Enabled, makes application access during reauthentication bypass Private Access, and is the API field `bypassOnReauth`.

quotes: Bypass during Reauthentication: Choose whether application access during reauthentication bypasses Private Access (Enabled) or not (Disabled).

reauth-bypass-platforms.summary: Two live pages name different Client Connector platforms for Bypass during Reauthentication: the Defined Application Segments page (the newer revision) and the AI-Powered Recommendations page, which embeds a copy of the segment form.

quotes: This feature requires Zscaler Client Connector version 4.3 or later for Windows, macOS, and iOS.

positions.says: Bypass during Reauthentication requires Client Connector 4.3 or later for Windows, macOS and iOS.

quotes: This feature requires versions Zscaler Client Connector 4.3 or later for Windows and macOS.

positions.says: Bypass during Reauthentication requires Client Connector 4.3 or later for Windows and macOS, with no mention of iOS.

reauth-bypass-platforms.impact: Whether the setting applies to iOS clients is not settled; both pages give 4.3 as the minimum for Windows and macOS.

label-to-api-mapping.title: How the console Bypass options map to the API values ALWAYS, NEVER and ON_NET
label-to-api-mapping.blocks: reading a segment's bypassType as a console setting
label-to-api-mapping.detail: Unverified legacy statement: ON_NET means 'bypass only for on-network users'. No captured source maps the three console options to the three API values; the Terraform examples use NEVER without saying which console option it is. Compare a segment's bypassType with the Bypass option shown in the console for one segment of each kind.

always-across-different-fqdns.title: Whether Bypass Always outranks a more granular segment that has a different FQDN
always-across-different-fqdns.blocks: deciding between a wildcard segment set to Always and a specific-FQDN segment under it
always-across-different-fqdns.detail: Unverified legacy statement: if any covering segment has bypass_type Always, that segment wins regardless of specificity, including a wildcard segment over a specific-FQDN segment. The help states the precedence only when the same FQDN is defined in several segments. Test with `*.example.com` set to Always and `host.example.com` set to NEVER.
